title: Interactive Topology Explorer
category_reason: Pure point-set topology: separation axioms T0/T1/T2, countability, hierarchy of topological spaces; no AI/ML connection.
thesis: An interactive sandbox exploring the hierarchy of separation axioms in point-set topology, from T0 through T2 and countability conditions, showing how each axiom adds structure to the notion of topological 'closeness' and which metrizability theorems follow.
key_claims: T0 (Kolmogorov) separates points by open sets: for any two distinct points, at least one has an open neighbourhood not containing the other
T1 strengthens T0: every pair of distinct points can be separated from each other; singletons are closed
T2 (Hausdorff) requires disjoint open neighbourhoods for every pair of distinct points, the standard separation axiom for analysis
Countability axioms (first/second countable) are independent of separation axioms and control metrizability
The hierarchy T2 implies T1 implies T0, and second countability plus T0 implies metrizability (Urysohn)
methods_math: Point-set topology: separation axioms, countable bases, metrizability theorems, Baire category
visualizations: Interactive T0/T1/T2 sandbox with point-pair separation testing; hierarchy map of topological spaces; countability base explorer
internal_tensions: The sandbox simplifies infinite topological spaces to finite point sets, which can obscure the real strength of the axioms (e.g. every finite T1 space is discrete, so finite examples cannot distinguish T1 from T2).

title: Ich bin ein Token
category_reason: Main subject is how LLMs process text: token journey through BPE, embeddings, transformer layers, attention, and autoregressive decoding.
thesis: A first-person interactive narrative following a single token through the full LLM pipeline, from BPE tokenization through embedding, self-attention, feed-forward layers, to autoregressive decoding, making the transformer architecture tangible from the token's perspective.
key_claims: BPE tokenization splits text into subword units learned from corpus frequency statistics
Each token is embedded into a high-dimensional vector encoding semantic and positional information
Self-attention lets every token weigh its relevance to all other tokens in the context window via Q/K/V dot products
Multiple stacked transformer layers iteratively refine token representations through alternating attention and feed-forward operations
Autoregressive decoding generates one token at a time, conditioned on all previously generated tokens
methods_math: BPE algorithm, high-dimensional embeddings, attention (Q/K/V dot products), softmax, feed-forward networks, autoregressive generation
visualizations: Token journey animation through pipeline stages; attention weight heatmap; embedding space projection; layer-by-layer representation evolution
internal_tensions: The first-person narrative anthropomorphizes a token, which risks implying intentional information flow where there is only linear algebra and matrix multiplication.

title: Holografische Entzerrung bei d=3 Grokking
category_reason: Investigates grokking (delayed generalization) in neural networks using Fourier analysis and Gram-matrix algebra at dimension d=3.
thesis: Squeezes a Fourier-based algorithmic understanding of grokking to the minimal dimension d=3, showing how the Gram matrix of training-set Fourier components controls the phase transition from memorization to generalization, and maps the result back to a 3D visualization.
key_claims: Grokking is a phase transition in the loss landscape triggered by weight decay and continued training past memorization
In d=3 the Gram matrix of the training set's Fourier feature components has eigenvalues that control the critical training step at which generalization begins
The 'holographic' de-squeeze maps the high-dimensional grokking picture to 3D without losing the phase-transition structure
Generalization onset time scales with the condition number of the feature Gram matrix
methods_math: Fourier feature analysis, Gram matrix eigenvalue decomposition, phase transitions in loss landscapes, weight decay regularization
visualizations: 3D phase-transition surface; Gram-matrix eigenvalue evolution plot; loss landscape cross-sections before and after grokking
internal_tensions: Reducing to d=3 necessarily loses the spectral richness of realistic feature spaces; the 'holographic' mapping is an analogy for visualization, not a proven equivalence to the full-dimensional picture.

title: LLM as Fibre Bundle
category_reason: Proposes a differential-geometric framework for understanding LLM layers as fibres over a base manifold, with holonomy and parallel transport.
thesis: Frames an LLM as a fibre bundle where each layer is a fibre over a base manifold of input contexts; the Jacobian of layer transitions defines a connection whose holonomy around loops in context space measures context-dependent meaning drift.
key_claims: LLM layers can be viewed as fibres over a base manifold of input contexts
The Jacobian of each layer transition defines a connection form on the bundle
Holonomy around a closed loop in context space measures how meaning is twisted after a context-dependent round trip
Parallel transport along a path in context space defines what 'the same meaning' means across different layers
Non-trivial holonomy is a geometric signature of the model's compositional depth
methods_math: Fibre bundle theory, connection forms, parallel transport, holonomy, Jacobian matrices, differential geometry
visualizations: Fibre bundle diagram over base manifold; holonomy loop animation; parallel transport vector field; layer-transition Jacobian heatmap
internal_tensions: The fibre-bundle analogy is mathematically rich but the 'base manifold' of contexts has no canonical metric; the connection is defined post-hoc from trained weights rather than derived from first principles.

title: Transformer Residual Stream Dynamics
category_reason: Analyzes the residual stream of transformers as a discrete dynamical system using Jacobian eigenvalue spectra and non-normal matrix theory.
thesis: Treats the transformer's residual stream as a discrete-time dynamical system where depth is the time index; the Jacobian eigenvalue spectrum (98% complex-conjugate pairs) and the strong non-normality of the iteration matrix control how information is rotated, amplified transiently, and eventually dissipated through layers.
key_claims: The residual stream evolves as a discrete dynamical system x_{l+1} = x_l + F_l(x_l) with depth as the time index
The Jacobian matrix of the full iteration has 98% complex-conjugate eigenvalue pairs, indicating dominant rotational dynamics
The iteration matrix is strongly non-normal: the spectral radius underestimates transient amplification
Transient growth visible in the pseudospectrum explains how small early-layer perturbations can be amplified before eventual decay
The balance between rotational and dissipative components controls how much signal survives to the output layer
methods_math: Discrete dynamical systems, Jacobian eigenvalue analysis, non-normal matrix theory, pseudospectrum, transient growth
visualizations: Eigenvalue spectrum plot in the complex plane; pseudospectrum heatmap; residual stream trajectory through layers; transient amplification curve
internal_tensions: Linearizing around a single trajectory ignores the high-dimensional nonlinearity of attention; the 'time' interpretation of depth is a metaphor that breaks down when skip connections create non-Markovian dependencies.

title: FRANKREICH ERLEBEN
category_reason: Interactive cultural and geographic exploration of France; no AI/ML content.
thesis: An interactive, visually rich scroll-driven exploration of French culture, geography, and history, presenting the tension between Paris-centric modernity and regional tradition through maps, cultural highlights, and narrative sections.
key_claims: France's cultural identity is shaped by the tension between Paris-centric modernity and regional tradition
Geographic diversity (Alps, coast, plain) directly drives culinary and architectural regionalism
The French Revolution's centralization created both national unity and lasting regional resistance
Cuisine, language, and landscape are interlocking systems that define French self-understanding
visualizations: Interactive map of French regions; scroll-driven narrative sections; cultural highlight cards
internal_tensions: The piece romanticizes regional diversity while its centralization narrative acknowledges the suppression of that diversity; the balance between celebration and critical distance is uneven.

title: Die Monster-Gruppe
category_reason: Group theory: the Monster group, sporadic simple groups, and moonshine; no AI/ML content.
thesis: An interactive exploration of the Monster group, the largest of the 26 sporadic simple groups with approximately 8x10^53 elements, and its deep connection to the Monster moonshine conjecture linking finite group representation theory to the modular j-invariant.
key_claims: The Monster group has approximately 8x10^53 elements and is the largest sporadic simple group
The Monster moonshine conjecture (Conway, 1979) states that the Monster's representation theory is encoded in the Fourier coefficients of the j-invariant
Moonshine was proven by Borcherds (1992) via vertex operator algebras
Sporadic simple groups are 'accidental' simple groups fitting no family pattern; their existence remains mysterious
The Monster's smallest non-trivial irreducible representation has dimension 196,883
methods_math: Finite group theory, sporadic simple groups, modular forms, vertex operator algebras, representation theory
visualizations: Group order comparison chart; moonshine coefficient plot; representation dimension chart; sporadic group classification tree
internal_tensions: The moonshine connection is deeply mysterious: the proof works but no one fully understands why the Monster and the j-function should be related; the file may present this as more settled than the underlying mystery warrants.

title: Finnegans Wake — A Visual Journey
category_reason: Literary analysis of James Joyce's Finnegans Wake; no AI/ML content.
thesis: A visual interactive journey through James Joyce's Finnegans Wake, mapping its Viconian cycle of history (genesis, climax, decline, dissolution, renewal), its network of recurring character-types, and its multilingual wordplay as the primary meaning-generating mechanism.
key_claims: Finnegans Wake is structured around Giambattista Vico's cycle of history: genesis, climax, decline, dissolution, and renewal
The Wake's characters are not individuals but recurring types that merge and split across the cycle
Joyce's multilingual puns (often spanning 5-10 languages per passage) are the primary meaning-generating mechanism
The text resists linear reading: it is designed to be read in loops, with the end feeding back into the beginning
visualizations: Viconian cycle diagram; character network graph; multilingual wordplay explorer; chapter and section navigation
internal_tensions: The piece must balance scholarly rigor (Vico, Joyce criticism) with accessibility for readers who have not read the Wake; the Viconian reading is one interpretation among several competing frameworks.

title: AEP & Shannon–McMillan–Breiman
category_reason: Ergodic theory and information theory: the asymptotic equipartition property and the Shannon-McMillan-Breiman theorem; pure math and probability, no AI/ML focus.
thesis: An interactive exploration of the asymptotic equipartition property (AEP) and the Shannon-McMillan-Breiman (SMB) theorem, showing how the per-symbol information concentrates around the entropy and why this underpins the theory of lossless source coding.
key_claims: The AEP states that for an i.i.d. source, the per-symbol information -(1/n) log P(X^n) concentrates around the entropy H(X)
The SMB theorem extends the AEP from i.i.d. sources to stationary ergodic processes
The typical set, sequences whose per-symbol probability is close to exp(-nH), contains nearly all probability mass for large n
This concentration is the mathematical foundation of lossless compression: only typical sequences need to be described
The rate of concentration is governed by the entropy variance in the i.i.d. case or by mixing conditions in the ergodic case
methods_math: Ergodic theory, information theory, entropy, typical sets, law of large numbers for stationary processes
visualizations: Typical set probability mass plot versus n; per-symbol information histogram converging to entropy; AEP concentration illustration
internal_tensions: The SMB theorem requires ergodicity, which is difficult to verify in practice; the i.i.d. AEP is easy to state but often too restrictive for real-world sources with long-range dependence.

title: Tropische Geometrie tiefer Netze — Einfach erklärt
category_reason: Applies tropical geometry (piecewise-linear structure) to deep neural networks; the main subject is neural network architecture understood through a mathematical lens.
thesis: Deep neural networks with piecewise-linear activations (ReLU) define tropical rational maps; the tropical geometry of the weight space, in particular the hyperplane arrangements and tropical varieties, controls the network's piecewise-linear complexity, capacity, and identifiability.
key_claims: A ReLU network computes a piecewise-linear map whose regions of linearity are cones in a tropical hyperplane arrangement
The number of linear regions (piecewise-linear complexity) is the network's geometric capacity
Tropical geometry provides the algebraic framework: the network map is a tropical rational map in the (max,+) or (min,+) semiring
Identifiability, when two weight configurations compute the same function, is governed by the combinatorics of the tropical arrangement
Deeper networks have exponentially more linear regions than wider shallow networks of the same parameter count
methods_math: Tropical geometry, piecewise-linear maps, hyperplane arrangements, tropical rational maps, semiring algebra
visualizations: Piecewise-linear region coloring of input space; tropical hyperplane arrangement; depth versus linear-regions plot; weight-space identifiability diagram
internal_tensions: The tropical framework assumes exact piecewise-linearity; real networks often use smooth approximations (GELU, sigmoid) that break the combinatorial structure; the 'simple' framing may understate the algebraic complexity of the full picture.

title: HoTT Chapter 1: Type Theory - Visual Explorer
category_reason: Homotopy Type Theory Chapter 1: type theory foundations, dependent types, identity types, propositions as types; pure mathematical logic and foundations, no AI/ML.
thesis: An interactive visual explorer of HoTT Chapter 1 (Type Theory), covering the judgment system, dependent types as fibrations, type formers with the uniform FIEC pattern, identity types as paths with composition and inversion, and the Curry-Howard correspondence between logic and types.
key_claims: In type theory there is one basic notion, types, replacing the two-layer structure of set theory (first-order logic plus set axioms)
Judgmental equality is meta-theoretic and algorithmically decidable; propositional equality is a type whose elements are paths or proofs
Dependent types (Pi and Sigma) are interpreted as fibrations: Pi is the space of sections, Sigma is the total space
Each type former follows the uniform FIEC pattern: Formation, Introduction, Elimination, Computation
The identity type a =_A b is the type of paths from a to b, supporting composition and inversion, giving a groupoid structure
Curry-Howard: logical propositions correspond to types and proofs to terms (and -> product, or -> coproduct, forall -> Pi, exists -> Sigma)
methods_math: Type theory, homotopy type theory, dependent types, identity types, fibrations, Curry-Howard correspondence, induction
visualizations: Types-vs-sets comparison cards; fibration visualization with clickable fibres; type-constructor grid with FIEC detail panels; natural number induction sandbox; path canvas with refl/compose/inverse animation; Curry-Howard logic table
internal_tensions: HoTT's univalence axiom, identifying types with equivalences, is the headline result of the HoTT program but is not covered in Chapter 1; the title 'HoTT' may mislead readers expecting univalence when the content is pre-univalence type theory.

title: Die Grundprinzipien der Chemie – Interaktiv
category_reason: Interactive chemistry: energy minimization (Morse potential), electrostatics (Coulomb's law), octet rule (ionic and covalent bonding); no AI/ML content.
thesis: An interactive exploration of three fundamental chemistry principles: energy minimization via the Morse potential, electrostatics via Coulomb's law, and the octet rule via ionic and covalent bonding, unified under the claim that chemistry is the redistribution of electrons to minimize energy and maximize electrical stability.
key_claims: Chemical bonds form because the bound state has lower total energy than the separated atoms, visualized as a ball rolling to the Morse potential minimum
Electrostatics (Coulomb's law) governs all chemical behavior: attraction of opposite charges and repulsion of like charges
The octet rule is the driving force for bonding: atoms transfer (ionic) or share (covalent) electrons to fill their valence shell
Polarity arises from unequal sharing due to electronegativity differences, as illustrated by H2O
The three principles are hierarchical: electrostatics underlies energy minimization, which underlies the octet rule as an emergent pattern
methods_math: Morse potential, Coulomb's law, electron shell model, electronegativity, ionic and covalent bonding
visualizations: Morse potential energy curve with animated ball rolling to minimum (Plotly); 2D Coulomb field with clickable charges, force vectors, and field lines (canvas); octet rule atom animation for NaCl, O2, H2O, LiF with electron transfer and sharing (canvas)
internal_tensions: The octet rule is a heuristic that fails for many molecules (BF3, SF6, transition-metal complexes); the file presents it as a fundamental principle, which is pedagogically useful but chemically incomplete.

title: Die Illusion erklärender Tiefe — Interaktive Reise
category_reason: Cognitive science: the illusion of explanatory depth (Rozenblit & Keil 2002), 12 studies, miscalibration, hierarchical systems; no AI/ML content.
thesis: An interactive journey through the 12 studies of Rozenblit & Keil (2002) on the illusion of explanatory depth: people systematically overestimate how deeply they understand causal-mechanistic knowledge, and the main driver is confusing environmental support (visible parts) with internal mental representation.
key_claims: The T1-T5 paradigm (rate, explain, diagnose, read expert text, re-rate) reveals a reliable drop in self-rated understanding after attempting to explain
The illusion is specific to explanatory knowledge: devices and natural phenomena show large drops; facts, narratives, and procedures show little or none
The strongest predictor of overconfidence (R-squared = 0.47) is the ratio of visible to hidden parts of a device
Three confusions drive the illusion: environment vs. representation, level vs. level (function is not mechanism), label vs. mechanism
The illusion may be adaptive: it acts as a governor that stops the potentially infinite search for deeper understanding once a good-enough level is reached
methods_math: Repeated-measures ANOVA, eta-squared effect size, miscalibration curves, multiple regression analysis
visualizations: 10-second self-test; ANOVA simulation (effect size, noise, sample size sliders); calibration curve with overconfidence bias; hierarchical system tree (clickable nodes); change-blindness demo; study T1-T5 trajectory plots; domain comparison plot; predictor scatter with regression line; three-confusion mini-canvases; final bar chart of illusion strength by domain
internal_tensions: The file uses synthetic random data for the predictor scatter in Study 12 rather than the actual device data from the paper; the R-squared = 0.47 is cited as the paper's result but the individual data points are randomly generated on each load.

title: Euklids Elemente - Interaktive Visualisierung
category_reason: Euclid's Elements: axioms, postulates, proof methods, constructions, proportions, philosophy; pure classical geometry, no AI/ML.
thesis: An interactive visualization of Euclid's Elements (c. 300 BC), the first fully axiomatic-deductive system in history: from 5 postulates, 5 axioms, and 23 definitions to 465 propositions in 13 books, culminating in the construction of the five Platonic solids, with emphasis on the parallel postulate, Eudoxus's proportion theory, and the strict 6-part proof schema.
key_claims: Euclid's Elements is the first completely axiomatic-deductive system: 5 postulates + 5 axioms + 23 definitions yield 465 propositions across 13 books
The 13 books form an ascending spiral from planimetry (I-VI) through number theory (VII-IX) and irrationals (X) to solid geometry (XI-XIII)
The parallel postulate (P5) resisted proof for 2000 years; its independence led to non-Euclidean geometries (Lobachevsky, Bolyai, Riemann)
Eudoxus's proportion theory (Book V) solves the problem of irrational ratios and is equivalent to Dedekind's cut definition of the real numbers, 2200 years later
Existence is proved by construction with compass and straightedge only, a form of constructive mathematics
The 6-part proof schema (Protasis, Ekthesis, Diorismos, Kataskeue, Apodeixis, Symperasma) is strictly formal and repeated in every proposition
methods_math: Axiomatic-deductive geometry, compass-and-straightedge constructions, Eudoxus proportion theory, exhaustion method, elementary number theory
visualizations: Sunburst chart of the deductive system; Sankey diagram of inter-book dependencies; bar chart of propositions per book; treemap of book sizes; radar chart of proof-method frequency; Eudoxus proportion line chart; historical timeline of Greek mathematicians; interactive construction canvas (equilateral triangle I.1, angle bisector I.9, perpendicular I.11); geometric algebra canvas with ratio slider showing (a+b)^2 decomposition
internal_tensions: The file presents Euclid's system as clean and complete, but modern logicians have identified implicit gaps (continuity assumptions, the 'obvious' cases in Book I proofs); the strictly constructive reading is one interpretation, and Euclid may have been less formal than the 6-part schema suggests.
